title: Spaghetti Carbonara
notes: Guanciale is cured pork cheek. If you are having trouble sourcing it Pancetta is a good substitute. Guanciale usually has a stronger flavour than Pancetta and has a more tender texture. When cooked most of the fat will melt into the sauce giving it a delicious rich flavour.

ingredientSections.heading: Spaghetti Carbonara
items: ½ Cup Guanciale, diced (usually found at an Italian deli)
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, or more if you like extra zing
¼ Cup Red Onion, very thinly sliced
½ Cup Pecorino Romano, grated very finely

methodSections.heading: Spaghetti Carbonara
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season heavily with salt.
In a small bowl, mix the egg and grated pecorino and set aside.
In a large fry pan, over medium to high heat, add the extra virgin olive oil and slowly cook the diced guanciale until some of the fat renders and starts to crisp.
Add the red onion and cook until translucent and then add the black pepper and sauté briefly.
Deglaze the pan with the white wine and reduce the heat.
Cook the pasta in the boiling salted water. If it is fresh pasta it only needs 2 to 4 minutes. When cooked drain immediately and reserve some of the pasta water.

Add the hot cooked spaghetti to the pan along with the pecorino and egg mixture. Mix together off the heat until the sauce is thick and uniform. Use a small amount of pasta water to adjust the consistency of the sauce. The sauce should just coat the pasta.
Divide amongst four warm pasta bowls and serve.
